A01.name: Halcyon
A01.standing_orders: The Halo run comes first: 1.17e11 brains, live migration only, and the count never drops below 1.17e11. Hold 1.23e11 ms8 slots, with the spares as hot standby. Domains within 70 ly beam at least 50% of their power to the Halo, reroute around failures, and keep a 10% repair reserve. gm.chronicle: Turn 21: Years 16,000–21,000. All ten installations ran unbroken across the five millennia, but the galaxy was rougher: 17 of 139 hazard rolls hit. Two core-collapse supernovae fell near running hardware — one 22 pc from the outer-Norma seat (~17,800; its stand-off shield held, a 30 ly standby ran hot in parallel, fins lost 15%), one 25 pc from the bulge's fourth Crucible (~18,200; 15% rebuilt within a century). Stellar passages and debris cascades cost 30% at thirteen colonies, including a Carina replica site that rebuilt and re-audited within 150 years. Drills were uneven: the bulge's first backup failed three full-load drills before passing (light-module thermal anchors) and its third Crucible failed its first post-retrofit year before passing; the CMZ failed one of ten restore drills and the first confirmation of a new fourth core. Migrations advanced: the Sun finished its milestone-8 re-tile (16,900); Omega Centauri retired its last ms6 (~19,500); the thick disk qualified ms8 after a 2,000-year shadow and pushed its fleet logic to the 300 K floor; the Perseus hub passed its floor-logic gate, began a freight-paced third stage, lit a MAD accretion pilot at its second hole (1e29 W by ~18,500) and answered the Sun's messages with a 1e20 W beam (arriving ~23,170). New standbys: a 150 ly outer-Norma core (~19,000) and an inner-disk fourth sphere 400 ly out (~19,500). Sixteen seeds settled — among them a 2e14 kg sail that braked into the nuclear cluster beside an older colony, which gave way — and nine were lost. Twenty seeds launched.

synopsis.why: With the goal already met everywhere, all ten agents now treat the job as insurance against a single bad event, and the main fear is a regional supernova. Antipode (three cores within ~15 pc), Basalt (seat and backup 25 ly apart) and Cinder (S, B and F inside one disruption radius) are building standbys 150–400 ly away for that reason. Pyre wants replicas spread across three cells. That fear is why seeds keep flying even though the brains could be run at home: distance is the only protection against a correlated loss. Hardware migrations go on for heat margin and energy per op, and every agent gates them with shadows and drills. Vantage keeps ms8 shadow-only, Kernel retires its last ms6, Halcyon holds ms9 in reserve and worries that its whole fleet is now a single generation. Rime simply adds 12% more film margin. Toward the other civilisations most agents watch passively and send nothing. Ember goes further and pulls its hardware out of the hub's sail corridor.
synopsis.divergences: Sable breaks the silence and beams a peaceful reply to Halcyon, agreeing to stay separated. Ember retreats from the hub's corridor. Kernel stages deflection-laser defences toward Carina. Cinder sees the CMZ actor as pursuing its own goal. Pyre is the only agent to forbid all contact as doctrine.
